To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel real-time monocular RGB approach to 3D human pose estimation, that is quantitatively competitive with the state of the art, and that is qualitatively comparable and often better than the best RGB-D solutions, and that works for a wide variety of real-world scenes and camera settings.
we are the first to present a real-time monocular RGB approach that is competitive with the best offline monocular methods, and that our results are qualititatively comparable to RGB-D methods.

we present the first real time monocular RGB method that is accurate and stable enough to enable 3D character animation, and that our method outperforms all existing monocular RGB methods on a variety of datasets, and is more broadly applicable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of 3D human pose estimation from a single image, and we present the first real time solution to this problem.
the problem of real-time 3D human pose estimation from monocular RGB video.
the following question: how to obtain a temporally consistent 3D pose estimate in real time from a single commodity RGB camera?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the first to enable real-time, accurate, temporally stable, and globally consistent 3D human pose estimation with a single RGB camera.
we present the first method that is capable of capturing the full 3D pose of a human using a single commodity RGB camera in real-time.
we are the first to provide a real-time solution to the 3D pose estimation problem for a single RGB camera.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to provide a real-time monocular RGB approach that can be used to capture 3D human motion data for real-time 3D applications.
we have developed the first real-time 3D pose estimation system that is applicable to a large set of real-world conditions.
we are the first to achieve real-time monocular RGB 3D pose estimation with the accuracy and robustness of state-of-the-art monocular RGB-D solutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single RGB camera can be used in real-time to obtain a temporally stable and accurate 3D human pose.
monocular RGB pose tracking can be done in real time with a single RGB camera---thus making it possible to use this modality for real-world applications.
real-time 3D human pose estimation from a single RGB camera is now possible, and that this capability opens up new applications.
